correctness.rationale: The orthonormal biased first-chaos coordinates yield kernel K_c(x,y)=sum c_i chi_i(x)chi_i(y). Its complex L-infinity operator norm is max_x E|K_c(x,Y)| by phase selection. At rare input coordinate x_i=r_i, the factor chi_i(x_i)chi_i(Y) equals U=(Z-a)/a with endpoint values -1,(1-a)/a; at common input it equals V=-(Z-a)/(1-a), a centered variable contained in the same interval. The secant bound for every convex t→|s+c_i t| (including complex c_i) gives E|s+c_i V|<=E|s+c_i U|. Independent coordinate replacements therefore monotonically increase row norm and make the universal rare vertex optimal for every diagonal multiplier. Adjoint argument supplies L1 norm; binomial centered first absolute moment telescopes to 2n(1-a) P(B_(n-1)=floor na), Gaussian CLT and fixed c/n Poisson local limit are correctly scoped. Independently enumerated all rows n=1..5 for heterogeneous rational coefficients and 27 exact binomial norm cases.
residual_risks: Only first homogeneous chaos and product strictly positive two-point measures; no assertion about minimal projection among all maps or higher chaos.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Defant et al treat translation-invariant Walsh projections on uniform Boolean cubes and can cover homogeneous a=1/2 first degree when symmetry makes rows equivalent. Product measures with unequal biases lose group invariance; Defant statements do not cover every complex multiplier and common minority extremal input. Nayar treats biased Fourier functions but proves FKN L2 stability, not endpoint norm maximization.
